findings.description: publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database to untrusted networks and relying only on security group rules and the master credential for protection.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume, snapshots and automated backups, so catalog data is stored in cleartext on disk.

The master password is supplied via var.password and the master username is the predictable default 'admin'. The password is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state and re-used in EC2 user_data rather than being generated/managed through Secrets Manager (manage_master_user_password).

user_data interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is readable in cleartext from the instance metadata service by any process on the host or via SSRF in the PHP app, leaking database master credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available. An SSRF in the hosted PHP application can retrieve the instance profile credentials (which hold s3:*, ec2:*, rds:* on all resources) and the DB password embedded in user data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the root volume holding dbinfo.inc with the database master password may be created unencrypted depending on account defaults.

The inline instance-role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", far beyond least privilege. Attached to an internet-reachable web server with IMDSv1 enabled, theft of these credentials yields near-total control of storage, compute and databases, including privilege escalation and snapshot exfiltration paths.
MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than scoped to the application server's security group, allowing any workload in the VPC to reach the database directly.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data exfiltration and C2 channel from a compromised database host.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set values and omits require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections; the generated PHP uses mysqli_connect() with no TLS options, so credentials and records traverse the network in cleartext.

The web server's only network control is aws_security_group.portal_sg, which is not defined in this file; the instance hosts an internet-facing PHP application with a highly privileged instance profile, so its ingress rules cannot be verified as restrictive here.
